name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090
summary: Ampere flagship with 24 GB of GDDR6X, still a favourite for local AI because of that memory. Projects you could apply to it: firmware updates, undervolting, open drivers and AI unlocks and deployments tuned for this card.

officialSupport.summary: in current drivers, no end date announced

models: Founders Edition from NVIDIA; partner cards (ASUS, EVGA, Gigabyte, MSI, Zotac and others) set their own connectors, power limits and vBIOS. The RTX 3090 Ti is a different card on the same die.

projects.name: gpu-unlock
projects.pitch: GeForce cards run FP16/BF16/TF32 tensor math at half rate; this kernel module removes the cap. Same results, faster: LLM prefill +25-55%, fine-tuning +25-50%, image generation +30-55%. Token generation and gaming do not change.
projects.suits: Long prompts, LoRA and fine-tuning, ComfyUI
projects.risk: Medium: a kernel module on the boot path, Linux only; remove the kernel option to roll back
projects.tested: Worked on ROMinit's own 3090 (2026-10-28): the kernel log reported the card unlocked after reboot.

projects.name: HyperQwen
projects.pitch: A vLLM setup for Qwen3.8-27B on one 24 GB card: 127 tok/s single stream, about 1,035 tok/s across 64 requests, profiles up to 240k context. Benchmarked on a 3090 at 250 W.
projects.suits: A private chat or API backend, long documents
projects.risk: Low: Docker, about 20 GB of model files
projects.tested: Ran on ROMinit's own 3090 with gpu-unlock at 240 W: prefill about 27-35% faster than an earlier baseline (not a controlled test).

projects.name: club-3090
projects.pitch: Community recipes for serving LLMs on 3090/4090/5090 with vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp and ExLlamaV3, for 1 to 8 cards, behind an OpenAI-compatible API.
projects.suits: Picking a known-good config instead of tuning your own
projects.risk: Low: Docker; read its CLIFFS doc on long-prompt memory failures

projects.name: NInfer-3090
projects.pitch: Native C++/CUDA engine with 3090-specific kernels and no Python at inference. Reports up to 140 tok/s for Qwen3.8-27B; speaks OpenAI and Anthropic APIs.
projects.suits: One model, one card, as fast as possible
projects.risk: Low: prebuilt Windows build; Linux is a community build

projects.name: llamAmpere
projects.pitch: llama.cpp fork tuned for Ampere: Qwen3.8-27B with 262k context inside 24 GB, about 103 tok/s at 100k depth.
projects.suits: Very long context on one card, llama.cpp tooling
projects.risk: Low: build from source with CUDA

projects.name: NVIDIA Resizable BAR update
projects.pitch: vBIOS update that lets the CPU map all 24 GB of VRAM at once, which some games run faster with. Also needs Above 4G Decoding and ReBAR on in the motherboard firmware.
projects.suits: Founders Edition owners; partner cards use their maker's tool
projects.risk: Low: official update; never use the Founders Edition file on a partner card

projects.name: NVFlash
projects.pitch: NVIDIA's vBIOS utility for Windows and Linux: back up the card's vBIOS, or write your board maker's official one.
projects.suits: Saving a backup before any firmware work, restoring one
projects.risk: High: a bad flash leaves no video; keep a second display output for recovery

projects.name: ReBarUEFI
projects.pitch: Patches a UEFI driver into an older motherboard's firmware to force Resizable BAR on when the board has no option for it. Makes no RTX 30 claim.
projects.suits: Boards whose maker ships no ReBAR update
projects.risk: High: modifies motherboard firmware; clearing CMOS recovers a failed boot

projects.name: LACT
projects.pitch: Linux GUI for power cap, clocks, fan curves and V/F-curve undervolting on NVIDIA cards. Less heat and noise at about the same speed.
projects.risk: Low: needs the NVIDIA driver with CUDA libraries

projects.name: MSI Afterburner
projects.pitch: Windows overclock and undervolt with a V/F curve, fan curves, OC Scanner auto-tuning and an on-screen monitor. Works with cards from all brands.
projects.risk: Low: download only from msi.com or Guru3D

projects.name: NVIDIA open kernel modules
projects.pitch: NVIDIA's open-source kernel driver for Turing and later, with the same user space as the closed driver. Its PCI ID table lists GeForce RTX 30 cards.
projects.suits: Linux users who want an open kernel module and keep CUDA
projects.risk: Low: remove other NVIDIA kernel modules first

projects.name: NVK (Mesa)
projects.pitch: Mesa's open Vulkan driver, conformant Vulkan 1.4, Kepler through Blackwell; OpenGL through Zink since Mesa 25.1.
projects.suits: A fully open-source desktop; CUDA still needs NVIDIA's driver
projects.risk: Low to medium: needs Linux 6.6 or newer and a recent Mesa

warnings: A vBIOS is board-specific: never flash one built for another board, including the Founders Edition one.
Resizable BAR also needs a compatible CPU, motherboard BIOS and UEFI boot.
gpu-unlock speeds prefill and training, not token generation; at stock power big matrix work gains less than the peak figure.
